column1: # THE CAP TABLE -- who owns the shares of the venture. Append-only.
# *** WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. *** The player, day 103: "let's track who owns the
# shares of the venture" -- alongside an inventory of what it holds
# (campaign/venture.tsv). The share structure has been sitting in
# campaign/wool_venture.md's prose since day 16 and has never been queryable.
# *** WHAT A SHARE MEANS HERE, PRECISELY. *** wool_venture.md, "The shares":
# capital returns off the top BEFORE anything is divided (CAPITAL RETURNS
# FIRST), and only the PROFIT that remains after that is split by share. A
# share is a claim on profit, not on the venture's capital or its physical
# stock -- campaign/venture.tsv answers what the venture HOLDS and OWES;
# this file answers who is entitled to a slice of what it EARNS.
# *** WHO HAS ACTUALLY PUT IN CAPITAL, AND WHO HAS NOT -- the player's own
# reckoning, day 103, and the reason this file does not try to price a share
# in gold: ***
#   THE PARTY  put in the 450 gp that bought the first lot (day 12-16) and the
#              288 gp that bought the second (day 73-83). ALL of the venture's
#              capital, both times, is the party's own coin.
#   WEND       put in no coin. She took a full share "backing her own
#              judgement" rather than the 20 gp fee offered (d6=1), and
#              separately contributes her shop and her barn and is paid for
#              her time -- a service, not capital. Her share is EARNED, not
#              BOUGHT.
#   THE HOLDERS put in no coin either. They chose "the floor price and a
#              share" over "a good price and no share" for their WOOL, which
#              the party bought from them AT THE FLOOR -- the wool itself was
#              a sale to the party, not an investment in it. Their share is
#              the PRICE of that choice, not a capital stake.
# So: 14 shares, one class, no capital weighting -- because no share was ever
# priced against capital put in. Pricing what a share is "worth" is valuation,
# and the player was explicit: figure that out when needed, not routinely.
# *** THE SIX HOLDERS ARE ONE ROW, `holders_six`. *** wool_venture.md names
# four of six by description -- "Rell's brother, Ellery, Marrow, Ferd's old
# master, and two more" -- and Rell's brother and Marrow resolve to people.tsv
# (gyll, marrow). The other two are NEVER NAMED IN THE RECORD. Splitting six
# shares across four knowns and two unknowns would invent an allocation nobody
# agreed to, which this project does not do. `holders_six` is a documented
# bucket, not a person, and it is closed vocabulary the same way `party` is in
# carry.tsv.
# who     a character name (characters.tsv), a people.tsv id, `holders_six`,
#         or `wend`.
# verb    anchor (sets outright) | move (adds, negative to remove -- a share
#         sold or transferred)
# shares  in units of a WHOLE share; Hask and Dellie hold half each per the
#         day-16 agreement (henchmen draw half where PCs draw full, the same
#         line characters.tsv already draws for experience and treasure)
